name: goap_packaged_loop_decrement_to_zero
mechanism: Extends goap_multi_example_composition.meta.json: after independently verifying (via real plan() calls, each in a fresh subprocess to avoid stale-fact branching) that the low-level primitive action 'decrement' reaches counter(Id,0) in exactly N steps for MANY distinct N -- including a held-back blind N never used to derive anything -- a new higher-level action 'decrement_to_zero' (precond counter(Id,X); effect counter(Id,0); cost 1, i.e. cheaper than N raw decrement steps) is registered via action_add. This packages the DISCOVERED repeated-composition pattern into a genuinely new, reusable, callable action, rather than leaving it as an unrolled N-step plan every time.
given_background: ONE generic primitive action 'decrement' (precond counter(Id,X)+pred1(X,X2); effects del counter(Id,X), add counter(Id,X2)) -- given background, same status as pred1/plus in earlier relational search work. The 'decrement_to_zero' action itself is NOT hand-verified for correctness against any specific N -- it is registered only after the raw mechanism's generalization was independently proven across many N first.
visible_verification: Raw 'decrement' alone (no shortcut registered yet) reaches counter(t,0) in exactly N steps for N in [1,2,3,4,6,8], each checked in an isolated fresh subprocess.
blind_verification: N=10, held back from the visible set, also reached in exactly 10 steps using ONLY the raw primitive -- before the shortcut existed.
acid_test: After registering 'decrement_to_zero' (cost 1, strictly cheaper than N raw steps for N>1), plan() was called for a BRAND-NEW, never-previously-tested value N=13. Result: plan([[counter,[t,0]]]) returned a SINGLE step, 'decrement_to_zero(Id=t,X=13)' -- not 13 unrolled decrement steps. This proves the packaged action is genuinely preferred by the planner's own cost-based search for an unseen input, not something declared and merely assumed correct.
sanity_check: An already-tested small N=3, re-run with both actions available, also correctly resolves via the shortcut (decrement_to_zero(Id=t,X=3)), confirming no regression.
provenance: direct response to: 'Let's do it!' following the confirmed multi-example GOAP composition capability and the user's original framing: '...we ought to be able to train it to do arbitrary loops even if it requires some more helper functions without going the whole hog of using extended cons...'
scope_note: This packages ONE specific discovered loop (repeated decrement to a fixed base case, 0) into a new action. It does not yet generalize to packaging arbitrary target values (e.g. 'decrement to ANY target', which was considered and deliberately rejected as it would be an unconditional jump declared to be correct rather than something proven by repeated-primitive search) or to loops over other primitive actions/domains.
related: spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_multi_example_composition.meta.json (the composition capability this packaging builds on)
